name: OpenCut
one_liner: A free, open-source video editor (like CapCut or Premiere, but you can run it yourself or build on it) that works in the browser, on desktop, and soon on mobile.
buyer: A content creator, small media team, or SaaS founder who wants CapCut-style editing but self-hosted, white-labeled, or embedded into their own product.
business_use_cases: A content creator studio self-hosts it to avoid CapCut's subscription fees and watermarks while keeping full control of their footage.
A startup building a niche video product (wedding videos, sports highlight reels) forks it and specializes the editor instead of building one from scratch.
An agency embeds the upcoming headless/API mode to offer automated batch video rendering as part of a content pipeline product.

money_ideas.idea: Build a hosted, white-labeled version of the editor for a specific niche (e.g. real estate video tours) and charge a subscription.
Once the plugin architecture ships, sell premium plugins (templates, effects, integrations) in a marketplace.

steal_this: This weekend, fork the classic version and ship a narrow, branded editor for one use case (e.g. short-form product demo videos) rather than competing as a general editor.
